King Bongani Ramontja (born 7 October 1985) is a South African community activist and civic organisation president. He is the founder and president of the Soil of Africa Advocacy Movement (SOA), a civic organisation involved in campaigns related to housing, service delivery, and community safety. Ramontja has been featured in South African media for his involvement in protests and advocacy efforts addressing housing allocation, relocation processes, and municipal governance in Gauteng.
Early life and education
Ramontja was born in Mamelodi West, Pretoria, an area that has historically experienced socio-economic challenges and service delivery protests. He attended Harvey High School, where he became involved in learner leadership activities. Details of his early education and student activism have primarily been reported through later media coverage of his community work.
Community activism
Following his schooling, Ramontja became active in community-based campaigns in Mamelodi focused on housing allocation and relocation processes, including matters related to Form C and RDP housing. He has been associated with protests and shutdown actions aimed at addressing alleged corruption and maladministration within the City of Tshwane Municipality.
Media reports have linked Ramontja and the Soil of Africa Advocacy Movement to campaigns calling for greater transparency in relocation processes and improved service delivery to affected residents. His activism has also extended to other townships in Gauteng, including Alexandra and Tembisa, where similar service delivery concerns have been raised in community actions reported by local and regional media.
Political involvement
Ramontja has been associated with political organising at local level and has previously been linked in media reports to activities involving the Economic Freedom Fighters (EFF), particularly in the context of housing-related protests and municipal engagement.
Soil of Africa Advocacy Movement
Ramontja founded the Soil of Africa Advocacy Movement (SOA), a civic organisation that has featured in South African media for its involvement in housing advocacy, community safety initiatives, and social issues. The organisation has called for increased police visibility in areas affected by violent crime and has engaged municipal authorities on service delivery matters.
SOA has also been involved in community outreach initiatives and public advocacy campaigns addressing youth welfare and local governance concerns.
African Native National Congress
Ramontja is associated with the African Native National Congress (ANNC), an organisation that describes itself as representing traditional leadership and indigenous governance interests. According to organisational statements reported in community media, he serves as its president. Independent national coverage of the organisation remains limited, and its activities have primarily been referenced in the context of advocacy relating to traditional leadership and land governance.
Ideology and public profile
Ramontja’s public statements, as reported in the media, have reflected positions influenced by Black Consciousness and Pan-Africanist thought, particularly in relation to land reform, community self-determination, and indigenous governance. His activism has received both public support and criticism, and he has been cited in news coverage concerning housing protests, relocation disputes, and community safety campaigns in Gauteng.
